headline: RL post-training enforces biological and physical validity in generative design models
label: Reinforcement Learning Biological Design
summary: Recent work applies RL with domain-defined rewards to virtual cell, docking, dosing, and molecular design models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reinforcement learning applied to biological models whose target properties are non-differentiable or set by domain constraints. CellFluxRL post-trains the CellFlux virtual cell image generator with seven biologically grounded rewards. A diffusion docking preprint fine-tunes DiffDock-Pocket on non-differentiable physical validity and interaction objectives. AI-MedCraft applies Pareto-guided RL with physics-aware scoring to multi-objective small-molecule design. OPTIMIS takes a different route: it compresses a hybrid Gillespie-ODE model into a differentiable Neural ODE digital twin, in which RL agents learn closed-loop dosing policies for an engineered cell model. What is new is the use of explicit, domain-defined rewards to enforce validity during model training or policy learning.
